assets.headline: An untested backup is a rumor.
If you can't export it, you don't own it.
Ask how long a full restore takes.
Close every login the day someone leaves.
Your domain belongs in your name.
Three copies. Two places. One offline.

beats: 1 CLAIM - the problem stated flat. No question mark. This is the feed thumbnail and does most of the work.
2 WHY IT HIDES - the mechanism that keeps the problem invisible.
3 DO THIS - one concrete action the reader can take this week. The screenshot slide.
4 THE CATCH - honestly naming what makes it hard. Earns trust and sets up the answer.
5 THE LANDING - one sentence where Bestly answers the catch. The ONLY slide that names the product.
rules: Device render appears on slides 1 and 5 only. Middle slides stay about the reader.
Slides 1-4 must be useful to someone who never buys anything.
Never more than 5 slides. Completion rate falls off after six.
One carousel per week maximum. Singles carry the other days.

carousels.hook: Nobody adds up the software bill.
You don't own what you can't export.
You may not hold all your own keys.
copy: You may not hold all your own keys.
Someone set it up years ago: the domain, the email admin, the website login, each made under whoever was helping that week.
Make a key list this week: registrar, email admin, web host, bank, payment processor, and whose name is on each.
Moving a key takes their help: most transfers need the current owner to approve, so do it while you are on good terms.
Keep the keys in your name: Bestly Cloud runs your files, calendar and passwords on a box you own, and the admin login is yours.

carousels.hook: When someone leaves, their logins stay.
copy: When someone leaves, their logins stay.
Every tool has its own admin page; turning off their email does nothing to the other apps they signed into with it.
Write a leaving checklist today: one line per tool, who removes access and how, run the day someone goes.
Shared logins can't be removed; the only fix is changing the password for everyone, everywhere it was used.
One place to switch someone off: Bestly Cloud gives each person one account for files, chat and passwords, so removing it once locks them out.
